subject: Post-call: unit-econ pathway & pricing band (tokens / feature)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@medloop.ai>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@medloop.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: unit-econ pathway & pricing band (tokens / feature)

Hi Samira / Alex —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have clear alignment on pricing sensitivity and the unit-econ view you asked for. I kept this high level and highlighted the assumptions we need to lock:

1) Volume profile: you described a ramp to ~3M tokens/day by month 9 (peak experimental usage in M9). You expect 40% of those tokens to be usage tied to the new triage feature.
2) Budget range: you mentioned a Q4 budget target of $80k-$120k/mo for inference costs; intent is to hold feature-level spend to <= $30k/mo in steady state for the triage feature.
3) Unit-econ asks: target $/1M tokens, $/feature (per MAU/feature-use), and CAC payback window (target 6–9 months).

What I attached: a starter unit-econ workbook (redwood_unit_econ_v1.xlsx) with three scenarios: conservative, expected, and upside. The workbook maps: tokens -> token-cost -> cost-per-feature (using your 0.4 feature share) -> margin at your projected price point (you mentioned $0.01–$0.03 per triage action to end users).

Immediate asks from us: can you confirm the expected % of tokens that will be billable (vs. cached/prefix) and an initial monthly MAU estimate for the triage feature? Those two numbers change the $/feature materially.

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm billable token fraction + MAU estimate (reply)
- Us: iterate the workbook and return a 2-slide summary with recommended target $/1M token bands and suggested pricing levers (batching, KV cache targets, quantization)
- Align on an internal pilot (POC) scope and SOW outline — I attached a draft SOW for procurement to review.

I’ll also get Marissa to sketch CAC payback scenarios linked to different pricing bands so we can see how discounts or committed capacity change payback.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Post-call: unit-econ pathway & pricing band (tokens / feature)

Thanks Ben — helpful recap. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Billable token fraction: we expect ~70% of generated tokens to be unique (billable) once the feature is live; we anticipate heavy reuse of templates so ~30% will hit cacheable prefixes. We can refine after a short instrumentation run.
- MAU estimate for triage feature: target 120k MAU by month 12, with a 7% weekly retention (this is our product target; we'll validate).
- Pricing to end customers: our PM is leaning toward a $0.02 per triage action list price, but we expect to offer enterprise customers volume tiers / seat bundles.

Request: can you produce the 2-slide summary you mentioned showing (a) target $/1M token bands aligned to $0.02/action, and (b) a CAC payback matrix for 6/9/12 month windows? Also please call out where committed capacity changes the outcome materially.

We reviewed the SOW draft and will share redlines by Monday.

Appreciate it — Samira

Subject: Re: Post-call: unit-econ pathway & pricing band (tokens / feature)

Hi Samira — looping in our pricing lead Karthik and sharing a few quick calculations below so you have an immediate sense before we finalize the slides.

Baseline assumptions (from Ben + your reply):
- Ramp to 3,000,000 tokens/day at peak (M9) -> ~90M tokens/month
- Feature share: 40% => 36M tokens/month attributable to triage feature
- Billable fraction: 70% => 25.2M billable tokens/month (triage)

Cost examples (approx, host-mode pricing bands):
- If $/1M tokens = $120 -> monthly inference cost for triage feature ~= $3,024 (25.2 * 120)
- If $/1M tokens = $600 -> monthly cost ~= $15,120

Mapping to $/feature: with 120k MAU and 1 triage action per MAU per month (conservative):
- 25.2M billable tokens / 120k actions = 210 tokens/action
- Cost per action at $120/1M = $0.0252
- Cost per action at $600/1M = $0.126

Implication: to hit your $0.02 list price per action and maintain margin targets (>50% gross margin on feature), target $/1M tokens needs to be roughly <= $100. That suggests either: a) commit to reserved capacity (dedicated) to get unit pricing closer to $60–$90/1M, or b) accept lower gross margin and use product packaging to pass partial cost to enterprise buyers.

Karthik — can you expand this into a CAC payback matrix (6/9/12 months) across three price bands (60, 120, 600 per 1M tokens)? I'll include these in the 2-slide brief for Samira.

Action items:
- Samira: confirm whether you expect >1 triage action per MAU/month (that will reduce cost/action)
- Ben/Karthik/Marissa: produce 2-slide summary + updated workbook by EOD Monday PST

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 10:22:00 +0530
Subject: Re: Post-call: unit-econ pathway & pricing band (tokens / feature)

Hi all — attaching a quick CAC/payback matrix excerpt (see Drive link in related_links). Key callouts below:

Summary table (high level):
- Price band A: $60/1M tokens -> cost/action ~ $0.012 (assumes 210 tokens/action) -> Gross margin at $0.02/action = ~40% -> CAC payback (120k MAU, ARPA assumptions) = ~9 months
- Price band B: $120/1M tokens -> cost/action ~ $0.0252 -> Gross margin at $0.02/action = negative (loss per action) unless you price higher or reduce tokens/action
- Price band C: $600/1M tokens -> cost/action ~ $0.126 -> not viable as list price unless heavily subsidized by enterprise seat revenue

Committed capacity impact:
- A 12-month reserved commitment reducing $/1M from 120 -> 60 flips the feature from marginal to healthy margin and shortens payback from ~18 months -> ~9 months in our model.

Sensitivity: if MAU generates >1.2 triage actions/month (multi-action users), cost/action drops proportionally and Band B becomes workable. Also caching improvements (raising prefix cache to 50%) cut tokens/action nearly in half.

Next steps:
1) Ben — share the two-slide summary with Samira today (I uploaded the matrix to the Drive link).
2) Samira — confirm expected actions per MAU and expected enterprise seat uplift (helps us map to ARPA).
3) Marissa/Karthik — prepare a short appendix showing how reserved capacity commitments and 6-month vs 12-month terms move the $/1M bands.

Cheers,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Pricing Analytics, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Post-call: unit-econ pathway & pricing band (tokens / feature)

Samira — attaching the 2-slide summary and a simple scenario table in the workbook. Highlights in plain language:
- To target $0.02/action with >50% gross margin we recommend considering a 12-month reserved commitment (target band: $60–$90 per 1M tokens) or pursuing feature packaging (bundle triage with seats so price per action is subsidized).
- If you cannot commit, the host-mode price band (~$120/1M) will likely make the triage feature margin-neutral or negative at $0.02/action unless you reduce tokens/action or increase list price to ~$0.04–$0.05/action.

Next steps from here:
- Confirm expected actions per MAU and whether you can trial a small reserved pilot (e.g., 3-month commit at modest discount)
- We’ll prepare a short procurement-ready SOW with an optional reserved pilot clause and sample pricing table to show how payback improves with commits

I’ll wait for your MAU/actions confirmation and your redlines on the SOW.

Thanks — Ben
